Planners sell a service area, not an address.

There is no shopfront to visit and no reason to want one. The work happens at your venue, on the phone and inside a shared document.

How does event planner coverage work in Australia?

Australian event planners work to a service area with a radius and go beyond it for a fee. The question that matters is not how close a planner lives to you. It is whether they have worked in your area before, and what they charge to get there.

Planner numbers follow event numbers. The six major markets below carry enough working planners that one brief can be quoted several ways. Everywhere else you are usually talking to planners who travel in, which is completely normal and should be priced openly rather than absorbed quietly.

Why we do not publish a page for every suburb

A page earns its place when there is a genuinely different planning problem to describe. The Northern Beaches has no train line. The Blue Mountains is cold, permitted and an hour past the last easy supplier. Fairfield runs 500 guest receptions as a matter of course. Those are real differences and they deserve real pages.

Manly, Cronulla, Marrickville, Castle Hill and Katoomba still do not get their own URLs, because the honest answer for each of them is already on the council or district page that covers it. Splitting that into five near identical pages would help nobody, and Google's spam policy names the practice directly.

Travel

What does travel add to the quote?

Three arrangements cover almost every Australian planner. Ask which one you have been quoted before you compare two numbers.

01

Included inside a radius

Most planners fold travel into the fee for anything inside their normal working area. Ask where the edge of that radius sits, because it is rarely written down.

02

A travel fee past the edge

Beyond the radius, expect a per kilometre rate or a flat charge per trip. Site visits are the trips that add up, so ask how many are included.

03

Accommodation for a distant event

For a regional or interstate event, a planner arriving the day before will usually pass on one or two nights of accommodation. It should appear as a line, not a surprise.

Ask for it in writing

A quote that says travel included is worth less than a quote that says travel included within 50 kilometres of the CBD, then $1.20 per kilometre. The second one you can compare.

Questions

Coverage questions

Do I need a planner based in my suburb?

No. Australian planners work to a service area rather than a shopfront, and the planner you meet in Parramatta is very often the same planner working in the Sydney CBD that month. What matters is whether they have worked at your venue or in your area before, and what they charge to travel. Ask both questions in the first conversation.

There is no page for my area. Can you still help?

Yes. The enquiry form is national and does not depend on whether we have published a page. Enter your suburb or postcode and the details go to planners who cover that area. We publish a page only where there is something genuinely different to say about planning there, which is why 22 places have one and several thousand suburbs do not.

Why is there one page per area instead of one for weddings and one for events?

Because a single page can answer both and two pages cannot answer either better. A wedding in Ryde and a company function in Ryde share the same venues, the same travel times, the same parking problem and largely the same planners. Splitting that into two URLs would put two of our own pages in front of one search, and neither would be as good as the one.

How far will a planner travel for an event?

Most metropolitan planners work a radius of roughly 50 to 100 kilometres without a specific travel charge, then quote beyond it. Regional and destination work is different again: a planner heading to the Blue Mountains or the Hunter Valley will usually build in a night of accommodation for a Saturday event, because a 6am finish and a two hour drive is not a plan.

Should I use a local planner or one from the nearest city?

Use whichever one has worked in your area, and ask each of them to name the last event they ran near your venue. A city planner who works your region every second month knows it better than someone who lives 10 minutes away and has never worked your venue. Distance is a cost question. Familiarity is the quality question, and they are not the same question.

Do you charge for the enquiry?

No. Sending an enquiry through Plan Your Event is free, and it does not commit you to booking anyone who replies. If you go ahead, you engage your planner directly and pay them directly. We are not a party to that agreement and we do not take a share of your planning fee.
